title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
`openexecutive.api.routes.today` serves the morning brief — a one-screen, read-only view of what is happening across the org. It is the default landing surface (the Next.js root renders `<Briefing>`). Every signed-in page shares one sidebar (`AppSidebar`). Its Recent list is capped at the 7 newest web chats. The full history, including Slack, Telegram and Discord conversations (recognised by their session-id prefix), lives on `/chats`. A chat opens from any page through `/?session=<id>`.

`GET /today` returns `TodayResponse` assembled by `_build_today()`, which is synchronous and caller-agnostic:

- **`departments`** — per-department goal health, rolling up each department's goal counts (`total`, `at_risk`, `off_track`) plus its awaiting-workflow count, and `attention_goals`: the actual off-track/at-risk goals (worst first, capped at 3) with `key_result`, `current`, `target`, and `status`, so the briefing's Department card shows *which* goal is off and how far without a click. Empty for healthy/inactive departments.
- **`people`** — an attention-ranked roster. Each person carries `awaiting_action` count, soonest SLA, a `status` (`on_leave` / `needs_reply` / `awaiting` / `clear`), reachability, `overdue`, a server `priority` sort key, and a cached one-line `insight`. Sorted by `(-priority, full_name)`. Stale insight notes are regenerated in the background only when the roster has more than one person: the UI shows the People sidebar only for more than one, so a one-person install (solo, or a team before anyone else is added) does not pay a daily model and peer-memory call for a note nobody sees. Cached notes are still served.
- **`proposals`** — the *live* unread alerts (workflow approvals, triage-classified inbound, Executive signals, flagged artifacts, and gated calendar bookings; an artifact carries `artifact_format` / `artifact_url` and a `body` already rendered to Markdown for its format, so the card badges it as a web page, Word doc, spreadsheet or link and offers *Open artifact*): unread, inside their category TTL, not snoozed — see *Alert lifecycle* below. Each carries `score`, `category` (`action` vs `monitoring`), `surfaced_reason` from `openexecutive.briefing.ranking`, the lifecycle fields (`occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, `last_reviewed_at`, `review_verdict`, `review_note`, `recommended_move`, `why_now`, `due_at`, `superseded_count`, `suggested_workflow`), and `decision_instance_id` (set only when the proposal is backed by a decision-ledger row — a calendar booking awaiting approval). The UI splits them into 'mine' vs 'across the team' using `caller_person_id`. For decision-backed proposals the card's Approve/Reject call the `/decisions` endpoints (which book or cancel the event server-side and clear the alert) instead of the ack-and-hand-off-to-chat flow — so meeting bookings are reviewed in the briefing itself rather than on a separate page.
- **`narrative`** — a per-viewer Executive-voice header synthesized by `synthesize_briefing_narrative`; the principal gets the whole-company scope, teammates a role-scoped one. In the web UI each bullet of this narrative is a click target: clicking one hands off to chat (the same `onContinue` path as the proposal cards) seeded to discuss that item. The Executive recognizes it because every chat turn now carries a `<briefing>` digest of open alerts (see Memory). That digest (`briefing.context.format_open_alerts_for_prompt`) is capped at 30 items; when the board is longer the header says so explicitly and tells the Executive to point at this page for the rest — it previously presented the capped list as the complete board, so the Executive described a slice as everything that was open (#136). Chat adapters get the digest too, but Slack gates it to the principal's DMs: the board is company-wide and must not be pulled into a shared channel. The `[alert_id]` at the start of each line is also what `ack_alert` trusts, because an id quoted inside an alert's own body came from inbound mail or chat and is attacker-controlled. This page's `[Discuss mode — alert_id=N]` handoff primer is a pointer to which item is under discussion, not authority on its own: the server accepts it only if that id is on the live board too. Two things enforce that. Every field the digest interpolates — headline, body, suggested action, tags, review note — is collapsed to a single line, since a newline in any of them would forge a whole extra `[N]` line and with it a fabricated instruction to clear someone else's alert. And the server records the live board it derived, so `ack_alert` refuses any id outside it — on **every** session, not just the chat adapters. The recorded set is the whole live board, not just the rows the digest printed, so a card past the render cap stays ackable. The control stops invented, closed, snoozed and expired ids; it does not stop the model being argued into acking the wrong *live* card. That check used to run only when `origin_channel` was set, which the browser never sets, so the one surface where the principal actually reads their board had no check at all and the model could ack any id, including one quoted out of an alert body by the Discuss handoff. Rendering the block and recording its ids now happen together in `briefing.context.render_and_trust`, which both the web chat route and the channel adapters call: render without recording and the tool refuses everything, record without rendering and the model gets reach it was never shown. A turn that was shown nothing trusts nothing. Recording it is only half the wiring: the tool reads the board off the turn's session through a ContextVar, and the chat route binds that session for the whole SSE body (`set_session`, next to `set_turn`). Bound from inside the Executive's own generator instead, it survives exactly one stream step — `asyncio.wait_for` runs each step in a fresh Task with a copy of the context — and the tool-call loop, which runs later, sees nothing. That shipped, and every web ack was refused on cards that were open the whole time. The digest also carries a short **already handled** tail — recently acked / dismissed / resolved rows, named but deliberately NOT trusted for acking — because a card cleared on the page minutes ago is otherwise simply absent from chat: asked to "record that as fixed", the Executive could not tell a settled item from one it had never heard of, and sent the principal back to dismiss a card that was already gone. That tail renders even when nothing is open, which is exactly when it matters. Note it is a different window from the `handled_overnight` rail above: that one runs since the last delivered morning brief, while the chat tail looks back 14 days (matching the action-alert TTL, so it still covers an item cleared late in its life), so chat can name a settled item the rail no longer shows. The narrative is held to what is **live**, and to what it is actually for. The `alert_raised` source is dropped from the activity it reasons over (`_build_activity(..., include_alert_raised=False)`): a closed alert reads as work the principal already settled, and a *live* one is worse than redundant — `lifecycle.is_live` is the very predicate behind `list_live_alerts`, so every live raise is already a proposal card below the header, which the prompt forbids re-listing. The `/today/activity` rail keeps the whole source, because a raise really happened. The activity block is only labelled "since last brief" when the caller bounded it with `since` (the standalone briefs do; the header does not), since calling an unbounded history rail a delta made the header present weeks-old rows as overnight news. When the viewer's slice holds nothing that wants a decision — no action proposal, no at-risk/off-track department, nobody awaiting — the regen skips the model call entirely and writes the fixed quiet line (`Quiet right now — nothing pressing.`, or `… nothing needs you.` for a teammate). **The cache key is a hash of the rendered context itself** (`today._narrative_context` builds it once and both the hot path and the background task key off that one string, which is also handed to the model verbatim). That makes the key a function of the model's input: everything the prompt renders is covered, and nothing it omits can trigger a regeneration. Keying on hand-picked fields broke one half or the other each time — headlines alone left the rendered activity block uncovered, while the proposals' review fields are never rendered by this header yet are rewritten with fresh prose by every `alerts.review` pass, so they regenerated each viewer's narrative several times a day to re-synthesize identical input. A quiet board keys off a fixed sentinel instead, so a moving rail cannot re-key an entry whose text is constant. Together: on a fully dismissed board every other input was empty, the rail became the only context, and the model synthesized a confident header out of closed items.
- **`in_flight`** / **`awaiting`** — upcoming Executive commitments and people we are waiting on.
- **`handled_overnight`** — the autonomous moves the Executive *completed* since the last delivered morning brief: the alert review's (routed, nudged, escalated, drafted, merged, closed) plus the research watch policy's (`watching` — a watch added on its own because it was grounded in company data; `stopped_watching` — a research watch auto-disabled as noisy or dead; no alert id, re-enable from `/watchlist`). A `changed` verdict (the review rewrote an open alert's headline / body / severity) is deliberately **not** here: the alert is still open in "Needs you" and its card carries the note, so the brief reports it under "what changed" (a REWRITTEN block) rather than as done. Each row is structured, not just a sentence: `kind`, the audit `summary` (nudge bookkeeping marker stripped), `at`, `alert_id`, `event_type` (for a pre-filtered `/audit` deep link), `headline` (the alert's headline at move time; a watch's slug), `target` (person name for routed / nudged, survivor headline for merged, new severity for escalated, draft title, workflow name), `detail` (the cited evidence or the watch policy's reason), `outcome` (`resolved` | `dismissed` for a close, `proposed` for a route that went through the authority gate), `evidence_ref` (S1 / R2 / A3), `superseded_by_alert_id`, and `status` — the alert's lifecycle state **now** (`open` = live in the queue per `lifecycle.is_live` | `resolved` | `dismissed` | `expired` | `merged` | `acked` | `inactive` for snoozed / past-TTL rows), looked up per row so a close the principal already undid renders as reopened instead of offering a second Undo, and a "still open" jump link only appears when there is a card to land on. The morning brief also carries a one-line count of research watch suggestions waiting on `/watchlist`.

The route resolves the caller from `x-caller-email`, then attaches the viewer-scoped narrative in a `BackgroundTask` so the request never blocks on an LLM call. `GET /today/activity` returns the recent self-initiated action rail — merged from fired scheduled actions (DMs, follow-ups, nudges, cadences), logged decisions, saved advice, completed workflow runs (briefings/check-ins/research), kicked-off initiatives, resolved gated decisions, and raised alerts, so it reflects all of the Executive's activity rather than just dispatched messages. The Pulse page (`/memories`) polls it (limit 100) every ~20s so new events stream into the 'Recent activity' card, which scrolls internally at a fixed height instead of growing the page. The `morning_brief` workflow calls `_build_today()` directly to build the standalone DM (via a different, enumerated prompt). `GET /morning-brief` is a deprecated alias.

**Solo mode in the UI.** The response is the same in both modes; the briefing reads the workspace mode from the app-wide `WorkspaceProvider` (which reads team while loading or on error, so a team install never flashes solo) and, in solo, drops the team surfaces: the Departments card, the People card, the "Across the team" lane (every action proposal is the one user's, so all of them land in "Needs you"), the people-awaiting, people-overdue and departments-at-risk status pills, and the quiet-day "Set up a check-in" link. A "N goals at risk" pill (at-risk plus off-track goals, from `departments`) links to `/goals` instead, so the strip never reads "All clear" over a goal that is slipping. In the Departments card's place, **Your projects** lists the initiatives with status `active` (`GET /memories/initiatives`): **Done** marks one `completed` through `PATCH /memories/initiatives/{id}` (only `completed` takes an initiative out of the Executive's active context), and **Drop** deletes it through `DELETE /memories/initiatives/{id}` after a confirm. The Pulse page hides its "Department check-ins" and "Awaiting people" blocks in solo, and its header shows active projects in place of the department check-in count. Team rendering is unchanged.

## Alert lifecycle & the Executive review

Alerts used to be write-once: raised, then never looked at again, so the "Needs you" queue grew without bound and the briefs re-listed it daily. Three things now keep it live:

- **Time-to-live** (`openexecutive.alerts.lifecycle`). Action items expire after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_ACTION` (14 d), unrouted low/medium monitoring signals after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_MONITORING` (3 d). Every surface reads `list_live_alerts` (the same predicate the scheduler's 15-minute sweep persists as status `expired`), so `/today` is right even before the sweep runs. Artifacts and decision-backed alerts are exempt. `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen` is the Undo.
- **Coalescing** (`alerts.pipeline` + `store.coalesce_alert`). A repeat of an open alert with the same `(source, dedup_key)` updates that row — `occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, severity max — instead of stacking a second card, and only re-pings when severity rose to high/urgent. Monitoring alerts carry a stable `watch:<slug>` key, so one watch means one card.
- **The review** (`openexecutive.alerts.review`, heartbeat `alert_review_scan`, every 6 h and right before the morning brief). For each open alert the Executive sees what changed since it was raised — newer signals from the same watch, related alerts, activity since, the roster with SLAs, department authority — and returns a verdict (relevant / changed / resolved / stale) plus a recommended move. Deterministic policy then acts: **route** (assign + DM the owner; `propose_via_alert` for propose-only departments), **nudge**, **escalate** (severity + `due_at` + DM the principal only), **draft** (`draft_artifact`), **suggest a workflow** (a link, never a run), **merge** (`superseded_by_alert_id`), or **resolve** — only on high confidence citing a server-minted evidence ref (a newer signal, a related alert, an activity item shown for that alert); free text never closes a card, and anything weaker is annotated `likely_stale`, demoted 30 ranking points, and left for one click. Everything that came from outside is rendered as inert data inside the review prompt, so an injected email body cannot steer the batch. Board / comp / legal matters only ever go to a scope-holder or the principal and keep their text. Route and escalate are idempotent across passes, every DM carries an "[Alert review] Re: …" header, outbound moves are capped per pass, passes are single-flight, `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED=false` stops every caller, every move is audited with its evidence and prior state, and a distinct `resolved` status keeps Executive closes separate from `ack` (user approved).

On the page, cards read as decisions: the one-line "what changed since you last looked" (`review_note`) leads, the recommended move is the primary control (Nudge <owner> → chat; Run <workflow> → `/jobs/<name>`), with chips for age, seen ×N, why-now / due, folded-in and draft-ready, a "Reviewed <ago>" footer, and an amber Likely-stale treatment with one-click Dismiss. "Needs you" shows *Start here* + 8 cards + "Show N more", a "Dismiss N older than 7 days" footer (explicit ids to `POST /alerts/bulk-ack` — never a server-side age sweep, which would hit teammates' routed items), and "Re-check relevance" (`POST /alerts/review`). The handled rail (anchor of the "Executive handled N overnight" pill) is deliberately one sentence by default: a first-person heading built from counts only — "Since your last brief: N off your plate (closes still standing, and merges whose survivor is not itself listed; a merge into a listed survivor counts on that survivor's row), N in others' hands (routed / nudged), N waiting on you (escalated)", plus "N drafts ready", "N workflows suggested", "N watch changes", "N other moves" (a kind the UI does not know) and "N back on your plate" (a close that is open again) when present — with the rows behind a "details" disclosure, and nothing rendered at all when the grouped rows are empty. The pure logic (grouping, headline, links) lives in `packages/ui/src/lib/handled.ts` and is covered by `npm test`. Expanded, it shows one first-person row per alert ("Resolved *X* — evidence", "Dismissed *X* as stale — evidence", "Handed *X* to Dana Kim" / "Proposed *X* to Dana Kim (awaiting their approval)", "Chased Dana Kim on *X*", "Raised *X* to high", "Drafted *T* from *X*", "Folded *X* into *Y*", "Started watching *slug*"), escalations first; rows sharing an alert collapse to the newest move with the others as an "also …" trailer — a close always keeps the visible slot (it carries Undo), otherwise an escalation beats routed / nudged / drafted; a merge whose survivor is listed becomes "N duplicates folded in" on the survivor. Every row links its `evidence_ref` (or "evidence") to `/audit?event_type=…&q=…` (the audit page pre-fills those filters from the query string), a still-open row jumps to its card (`#alert-<id>`), drafted rows link `/artifacts`, watch rows `/watchlist`. Undo is offered only while the close still stands (`status` not `open`); a reverted close shows "Reopened". Dismissing a watch-sourced alert lowers that watch's `trust_score` (which discounts ranking and is shown to the review as evidence); the ack body may carry `mute_topic`. Acknowledging or resolving an alert — including the review closing it itself — marks the review's DMs about it `acted` in the Attunement outcome ledger, for the person it is routed to and the principal only; dismissing it, finding it stale or letting it expire voids them (counted neither way). Review DMs are tagged `alert_review` with `alert:<id>`.

## Multi-client practice section

In multi-client practice mode (2+ client slots — see the Client Companies section), the response gains an additive `practice_clients` list: rollup cards for the **parked** clients (overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, onboarding due soon, renewal countdowns), each stamped with the save point its data reflects. Single-company installs always receive an empty list and the UI renders nothing.
